newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close lower in heavy red chip trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close lower in heavy red chip trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slid in late trade to close lower on Friday on heavy turnover as more investors abandoned blue chips in favour of the red-chip sector, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed 81.07 points or 0.64 percent lower at 12,645.76, near the day's low of 12,643.28. Turnover climbed to nearly HK$15.15 billion.
Hong Kong stock exchange figures show Friday's turnover to be provisionally the fourth heaviest ever.
Turnover on Thursday was also heavy at HK$13.51 billion.
"There is still concern about interest rates and interest rate sensitive sectors," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities.
Shum said the blue-chip index was down in line with the Dow's 20-point fall to 6,792.25 overnight.
Trading activity on Friday was concentrated in China concepts stocks, chiefly those that have acquired new operations or are likely to acquire assets from their parent.
"People are pricing in the asset injection potential of a company or its management," said Chris Geiger, associate director at Vickers Ballas.
"China Merchants Hai Hong has in one day acquired assets which double the size of the company," Geiger said.

Red chip China Merchants Hai Hong was the most actively traded stock. Shares in the company, which issued 650 million new shares on Friday to fund acquisitions from its parent, rose HK$0.70 to HK$8.55 on trade of HK$932.16 million.
Red chip and Hang Seng Index constituent CITIC Pacific put on HK$0.80 to HK$41.60. Analysts said the share is breaking out of its consolidation pattern and has good upside potential.
Blue chip Swire Pacific added HK$1.00 to HK$59.00, while banking giant HSBC Holdings, the second most actively traded issue, lost HK$1.00 to HK$189.50 on trade of HK$618.37 million.
The index's late slide was in line with trading in the April Hang Seng Index futures, which closed down 80 points at 12,645. The April contract expires on Tuesday.
